title: Influence of erector spinae plane block on perioperative pain management and hospital length of stay after thoracolumbar spine surgery
summary:
Complex spinal surgery causes postoperative pain. However, perioperative pain management is often inadequate and controversial. Opioids, which are traditionally used for pain relief, have side effects such as nausea, vomiting and respiratory depression. New ultrasound-guided nerve blocks such as the Erector Spinae Plane Block (ESPB) show promising results and represent a safe alternative. This procedure reduces pain, the need for opioids and the length of hospitalization.

The efficacy of the ESPB in relation to different surgical approaches and planes has not yet been fully investigated. The aim of this study is to evaluate the impact of ESPB on pain management and length of hospital stay after spinal surgery.

Patient-specific factors and the biopsychosocial pain model play an important role in the postoperative pain experience. The study focuses on perioperative pain management and preventive analgesia by ESPB in the first 24 hours after surgery.

It is expected that effective pain relief will lead to a shortened hospital stay. The study will also investigate the effects of ESPB on operation time, blood loss and treatment costs.

The implementation of ESPB at a university hospital will be studied specifically for trauma surgery and orthopaedic patients with spinal disorders.
conditions: Fracture of rib(s), sternum and thoracic spine
Fracture of lumbar spine and pelvis

interventions.name: Intervention group: Spinal surgery with erector spinae block (ESPB) [local anesthesia procedure].
control group: spine surgery without ESPB (standard of care)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Patients with traumatic injuries (e.g. vertebral fractures) and the consequences of injuries (e.g. post-traumatic misalignment) of the thoracolumbar spine
- Patients with degenerative spinal conditions (e.g. herniated disc, stenosis, etc.)
- Adults (≥ 18 years of age)
- Consent to the application of the regional anesthesia procedure
- Consent to participate in this study after detailed
Exclusion criteria:
- Inflammatory diseases and tumors
- Chronic pain syndrome with use of opioid painkillers for longer than 6 months
- Neurological deficit
- Contraindications for a peripheral regional anesthesia procedure (e.g. allergy to local anesthetic, infections in the puncture area, refusal by patient)
- Lack of consent to participate in the study
